data.narrative:
Electric Hydrogen, a Series C climate and energy company founded by Raffi Garabedian and David Eaglesham, is evaluated against a peer universe of five same-sector, similar-valuation-tier comparables spanning public and private markets. The comp set includes public names (QuantumScape at $3.6B, Enovix at $1.0B, Solid Power at $504M) and private peers (KoBold Metals at $3.0B, Amogy at $700M), establishing a range of $504M to $3.6B across the sector.

Two valuation methods apply to the $1.0B last post-money valuation. Stage-progression analysis, applying a typical 1.7x step-up multiplier for Series C advancement, yields $1.7B. Peer-median analysis across the five comparables produces $1.0B, reflecting the median positioning within the climate-energy cohort. These methods triangulate to a valuation range of $850M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median of $1.4B.

The analysis supports a fair-value band centered at $1.4B, approximately 40% above the current $1.0B post-money valuation. Key uncertainties include the timing and probability of next-stage funding, execution risk on hydrogen commercialization timelines, and potential re-rating driven by comparable company public market performance—particularly QuantumScape and Enovix, which exhibit wide valuation dispersion within the sector.
